definition: The abstract-noun view that things exist absolutely, named as one of the two extremes the middle-way teaching on right view avoids.
notes: An abstract noun formed from atthi (exists), distinct from the bare verb. Paired with natthita (the view of non-existence). Related to but not identical with sassatavada (eternalism) and ucchedavada (annihilationism): atthita/natthita name the view-poles directly, while sassatavada/ucchedavada name the doctrinal positions built on them.
